why_this_file_exists: Terms removed when the list moved from weighted scoring to a word search (schema 2.0.0). Under scoring these could corroborate another term without selecting anything on their own; under a word search every term selects, so a term that is not specific to plant protection selects the wrong cases. Kept here so a later curator can see what was considered and why it went.

terms.removed_because: Every chemical, pharmaceutical and food case names an active substance.

terms.note: Contextual: the NVWA appears across food and animal law. Only meaningful alongside a pesticide term. DOCUMENTED EXCEPTION to the acronyms-only rule; see 'Known exceptions' in the keyword README for the measured cost. Revisit under issue #24.
terms.removed_because: The food and product safety authority appears in every case it brings, on any subject.

terms.note: DOCUMENTED EXCEPTION to the acronyms-only rule; see 'Known exceptions' in the keyword README for the measured cost. Revisit under issue #24.
terms.removed_because: EFSA, ECHA and RIVM advise on chemicals, food and health generally, not on pesticides alone.

terms.note: DOCUMENTED EXCEPTION (docs/jurisdictions/nl.md 5.7, issue #57). Split out of nl-toelating, which it used to be an alias of, so that a gate could be put on it alone. 'Toelating' is admission in general and in Dutch administrative practice a toelatingsbesluit is overwhelmingly an immigration decision, so it no longer qualifies a document by itself: it needs a plant-protection word somewhere in the document, which the authority's own name - College voor de toelating van gewasbeschermingsmiddelen en biociden - already supplies. Same instrument as nl-drift. requires is an AND over one id (issue #24), so a biocide-only authorisation loses these three points and keeps its own weight-3 term.
terms.removed_because: An authorisation decision is an ordinary administrative act in every licensing field.

terms.note: DOCUMENTED EXCEPTION (docs/jurisdictions/nl.md 5.5, issue #57). regex rather than substring for one alias only: the bare 'kwekerij' now needs a word boundary on its left, so 'hennepkwekerij' no longer matches while 'kwekerij' and 'kwekerijen' still do. Every other pattern here is an unanchored expression and so keeps substring semantics.

terms.note: Homonym trap: 'drift' also means anger/impulse in criminal judgments. Only counts alongside a spraying term.
